Name writes accept a leaf name or a fully qualified name within the existing namespace; readback uses the fully qualified name and can be reused without adding namespace prefixes. Edits retain the current namespace; other namespace-like text remains literal leaf-name text. Regular comments map to PRE and inline comments to EOL at the exact function entry. Changes commit together after readback and refreshed analysis; failure rolls them all back.
Annotation text rejects NUL and unpaired Unicode surrogates before mutation, with the field and UTF-16 index in the error. Supported Unicode and line endings are preserved.

capabilities.reason: Binary Ninja MCP is not configured
limitations: The official Binary Ninja MCP server uses server-issued, session-scoped open-item and BinaryView handles. REA+ binds one view by its returned handle and revalidates its path and input SHA-256 around each normalized operation; image base is also revalidated when exposed by the installed overview tool.

The GUI server shares its active BinaryView with the Binary Ninja UI. REA+ may select the bound view to make official active-view tools target the admitted artifact; this changes server/UI selection but does not save, close, rename, or patch the user's database.

The normalized provider calls only allowlisted official read/query tools plus the open-item and view-selection tools required to bind the target. It does not invoke save, close, analysis-control, or mutation tools.

Function and string inventories, pseudocode, and assembly are Binary Ninja analysis observations, not original source. The installed official tool catalog and output schemas can change; REA+ reports an actionable compatibility error when required tools or fields differ.
Provider version identifies the REA+ adapter. Binary Ninja engine and MCP server versions remain the caller-supplied server's responsibility and are reported separately when available.

availability.reason: Set REA_RADARE2_PATH to the absolute path of a radare2 >=6.0.0 <7.0.0 executable (verified with 6.2.4) or a Rizin >=0.9.0 <0.10.0 executable (verified with 0.9.1); REA+ installs neither. See docs/radare2-provider.md.

capabilities.reason: Set REA_RADARE2_PATH to the absolute path of a radare2 >=6.0.0 <7.0.0 executable (verified with 6.2.4) or a Rizin >=0.9.0 <0.10.0 executable (verified with 0.9.1); REA+ installs neither. See docs/radare2-provider.md.
limitations: REA+ runs the caller-supplied radare2 executable (REA_RADARE2_PATH) in its documented -q0 pipe mode over a SHA-256-verified private copy of the admitted target, with user rc files disabled (-N) and cfg.sandbox enabled. radare2 never opens the original path, and REA+ never forwards caller text into radare2 commands.

Functions, names, strings, references and call edges are observations of radare2's selected analysis level (aa, aaa or aaaa), not original source. Indirect calls and references radare2 did not resolve are absent rather than proven nonexistent.
procedure_pseudo_code returns radare2's built-in pdc pseudo-code, an annotated low-level listing rather than structured decompilation. Use procedure_assembly when instruction precision matters.
list_strings and search_strings cover radare2's data-section string inventory (izj); an empty result does not prove the text is absent from the artifact bytes.
Procedure names keep radare2 flag prefixes such as sym., sym.imp., fcn. and entry0. Procedure arguments also accept an exact symbol name or a 0x-prefixed address.
Cancelling or timing out an in-flight radare2 command stops its process. The next operation starts a fresh process and repeats the analysis.
REA_RADARE2_PATH may instead name Rizin 0.9.x. Rizin has no command sandbox and no pdc pseudo-code; results then carry Rizin's limitations.
